summary.oneLiner: Ceeta Industries Limited, founded in 1984, is a diversified enterprise that has repositioned itself around FMCG, manufacturing packaged traditional and extruded snacks under its "Skitos" brand from a single plant at Tumkur, Karnataka.
summary.business: The Company manufactures packaged snack foods - traditional snacks, potato chips, extruded snacks, fryums and other snack products - along with fruit drinks in various flavours, sold under its own brand "Skitos". It also undertakes contract manufacturing for third-party customers, leveraging its manufacturing expertise and operational capacity. Products are positioned as quality offerings at competitive price points and reach consumers through a distributor-led network across multiple sales channels in India.

currentContext.expansion: Ceeta discloses no new plant, no greenfield project and no capital commitment for FY2025-26 - the named Capital Commitments disclosure states that "The company does not have any capital commitments in the current and previous year." Expansion in the year was incremental debottlenecking and modernisation at the existing Tumkur, Karnataka plant, described in the Section 134(3)(m) annexure. The largest item was the installation of 2 new modernised packing machines, which increased capacity from 10 tons per day to 12 tons per day. Other plant investments included a mezzanine racking system to increase storage, an online conveyor belt enabling online packing of potato chips (controlling material spillage and reducing manpower), online metal detection for product safety, a Vibro shaker (De-Oiling belt) installed across all pellet product lines at the units, a Potato Grader, an Air turbine, and a new SS Cylinder with Solenoid Timer. Utility and environmental infrastructure added or in place includes a 10 KLD sewage treatment plant whose treated wastewater is used for gardening and flushing, a 140 KLD ETP and water recycling plant recycling roughly 80% of discharged water, rainwater harvesting at the plant, VFDs on the air compressor, Trafo power-factor correction equipment, IE3 five-star motors replacing older heavy-duty motors, LED lighting, smart thermostats and panel-wise energy and line-wise water meters; the Company also uses bio-mass briquettes to generate process heat. The Company states that capital expenditure on energy conservation equipment is not separately accounted. Forward-looking intent is framed as strengthening manufacturing capabilities and operational efficiency rather than as any named or dated project.

risks.risk: Raw material and packaging input cost and availability volatility
risks.note: Management flags that volatility in the cost and availability of raw materials and packaging inputs can affect margins, and the SWOT lists volatility in raw material prices and dependency on the availability of raw materials at competitive prices. For a potato-chips and snacks manufacturer this is the primary margin driver; mitigation is limited to procurement optimisation, vendor relationships and alternate sourcing, with no hedging or pass-through mechanism described.

risks.risk: Intense competition from both organised and unorganised players, with limited product differentiation
risks.note: The Company competes in a fragmented FMCG snacks market against organised and unorganised participants, and its own SWOT records limited product differentiation in certain product categories as a weakness. That combination caps pricing power for a sub-scale player competing against national snack brands.

risks.risk: Dependence on third-party distributors for market penetration and reach
risks.note: Listed verbatim as a weakness in the Company's SWOT. Route-to-market is not owned, so distribution expansion - the Company's stated primary growth lever for the "Skitos" brand - depends on partners the Company does not control.

risks.risk: Manufacturing and supply-chain concentration at the Tumkur, Karnataka facility
risks.note: The Company's manufacturing is at a single stated facility at Tumkur, Karnataka, and management flags that operational disruptions or inefficiencies in logistics and supply chain can result in delays or increased costs. Mitigation is process reliability, buffer stocks where necessary and vendor contract review; there is no second site named to absorb a disruption.

risks.risk: Demand sensitivity to macroeconomic conditions and consumer spending
risks.note: Management flags that fluctuations in inflation, interest rates and consumer spending patterns can impact business growth, and the SWOT names sluggish or fluctuating consumer demand patterns as a threat. Persistent inflationary pressures on input and logistics costs are cited separately as a threat, so the Company can face weak demand and rising costs at the same time.

risks.risk: Increasing health consciousness shifting dietary preferences away from fried packaged snacks
risks.note: Named as a threat in the SWOT. This is the structural, secular risk to the product portfolio - potato chips, fryums and extruded snacks - rather than a cyclical one, and it is the risk least addressable by cost or distribution actions.

risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance risk around food safety, packaging and labelling
risks.note: The SWOT names regulatory changes relating to food safety, packaging and labelling requirements as a threat, and the secretarial auditor identifies the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006, the Legal Metrology Act 2009 and the Trade Marks Act 1999 as the laws specifically applicable to the Company. Non-compliance in a food business carries product-recall and licence consequences, not just penalties.

risks.risk: Technology and cybersecurity risk from increasing digitalisation
risks.note: Management flags that increasing digitalisation exposes the business to cyber threats, data security risks and potential system disruptions, addressed through IT security controls, data backup, access management and periodic monitoring.
